Subject: Pool topology & burst guardrails for Helio Health pilot

Hi Marta / Helio ops team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the pilot — excited to get the dedicated pool turned up. Attached is a draft pool topology (helio-pool-topology-v1.xlsx) and a short Mission Acceptance Plan (MAP-helio-dedicated.pdf) that outlines milestones. High-level proposal below: 

- Primary region: us-west1 (closest to your west coast infra); failover: us-east1.
- Baseline pool: 4 x A100-80GB nodes (32 GPUs total) for steady traffic; autoscale min=2 nodes, target nominal=4, max=8 for sustained demand.
- Burst: temporary expansion up to 16 nodes using preemptible capacity and cross-region spill to us-east1 when baseline capacity saturates.
- Autoscale triggers: a combination of sustained GPU util (65% for 3 min) and queue depth (requests waiting >200ms).
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 120ms for single-turn endpoints with caching; we’ll use prefix KV caching and request-level batching.

Open questions for you:
1) Is us-west1 acceptable as primary for data residency/compliance?
2) Any procurement constraints on preemptible/spot instances? (procurement@ copied)
3) Do you want a warm pool (kept hot) for critical hours, or prefer cold burst to save cost?

Proposed next step: 30-min tech handoff Wed 2026-05-27 10:00 PT to agree runbook and IP allowlist.

I’ve attached the topology and MAP for review. If that looks good I’ll route a netops checklist to your eng-ops alias and loop Ben for scaling tests.

Best,
Lauren

Hi Marta — great questions, answered inline below and in the updated MAP I’ve attached.

- Data residency: both us-west1 and us-east1 are US regions; we will ensure logs and long-term storage are kept in the selected region per the MAP (see section 3).
- Failover & caching: prefix/KV cache is regional by default. During cross-region failover we will:
  1) serve from read-only replicas in the secondary region for cold traffic;
  2) prioritize model parity by pinning to the same model artifact version (we replicate model artifacts asynchronously; short window for sync on a new rollout).
  3) expect a ~30–120s window for caches to repopulate after failover — we'll document an SLO for cache-warmup.
- Burst and model parity: burst uses the same model build; we’ll push artifacts to both regions before enabling burst. If you want zero-window parity we can hold rollouts during peak windows.
- Procurement: I added a procurement checklist in the MAP. Key ask: approval to allow preemptible instances for burst (cost-effective) and a signed addendum for capacity burst terms.

Ben will own the autoscale tuning and warm-pool recommendation; Monica will track netops checklist and kickoff scheduling. Proposed action items:
- Ben: recommend warm-pool size and scale triggers by EOD Tue.
- Monica: prepare netops allowlist + runbook for Wed tech handoff.
- Marta: confirm whether you want warm-pool for business hours or prefer cost-optimized cold burst.

If okay I’ll lock the Wed 5/27 10:00 PT slot with a calendar invite and attach the SOW stub for procurement to review.

Cheers,
Lauren

Lauren / Monica — quick internal notes on autoscale and warm-pool logic before we present to Helio: 

- Scale-up triggers: start a scale-up when avg GPU util > 65% sustained for 180s OR request queue length > 30 for 90s.
- Scale-down: reduce cautiously (hold 10m cool-down) to avoid thrash; prefer step-downs of 1 node at a time unless utilization drops < 20%.
- Warm-pool recommendation: keep a hot warm-pool of 2 nodes during 08:00–20:00 PT (Helio peak) to bring cold-start latency down; this adds ~12% baseline cost but reduces cache warm-up windows.
- Burst policy: prefer preemptible for cost; set auto-fall-back to on-demand if preemptible reclaim rate > 20% over a 10-min window.
- Network: need Helio netops to allow outbound egress to our model artifact S3 repo and a set of control-plane IP CIDR ranges (I’ll attach a minimal list).

I’ll prepare a short test plan: 1) synthetic traffic ramp to 2x predicted peak; 2) verify p95 latency and cache warm-up; 3) validate cross-region failover under simulated region outage.

Ben
